mentions.author: AareyBaba
mentions.story: An Interactive Introduction to Fourier Transforms
mentions.text:
I recommend Coursera Digital Signal Processing by Martin Vetterli [course]. He does a good job of explaining the math behind
the DFT. Any finite signal can be expressed as a linear combination of complex exponentials - that was the aha! moment for me.

Once you have that under your belt you might find
Audio Signal Processing for Music Applications by Xavier Serra a fun course to complete
[course].

mentions.author: viewtransform
mentions.story: A Pragmatic  Introduction  to Signal Processing
mentions.text:
I recommend Prandoni & Vetterli's coursera class on Signal processing[1].
They have really made an effort to teach this in an intuitive manner
instead of just throwing equations at you. This was the course where
I finally really understood Fourier transforms in a visual way.

The other course I recommend is the Audio Signal processing class by Xavier Serra[2]
This is a practical class with lots of hands on programming examples and introduction
to useful open-source software tools.

[1] [course]
[2] [course]

mentions.author: medymed
mentions.story: History and Derivation of the Fast Fourier Transform
mentions.text:
Is is just me being a n00b or are there a few errors in the equations? Like the exponential definitions of sin and cos, a missing negative sign in proof of m≠n, maybe more later not sure. Somewhat perplexing for someone learning the stuff BUT then again, I'm in medicine; so it might actually just be me.

Relevant for other learners is the digital signal processing lectures on Coursera, highly recommended with python notebooks and quizzes. [course]
